summaries.gardner: PMI is a market leader with strong brands (Marlboro, IQOS, ZYN) and strong recent momentum, but it is a century-old tobacco business in a shrinking cigarette industry rather than a top dog in an emerging one. Its smoke-free shift (41.5% of 2025 revenue) is the only Rule Breaker-like element, and it is not a disruptive innovator in Gardner's sense.
summaries.buffett: PMI has many Buffett traits: a simple, durable business, strong pricing power, 67% gross margins and free cash flow of $10.7B in 2025 (94% of net earnings). Against it are heavy debt ($49.1B) and a stockholders' deficit, a tobacco industry Buffett has historically avoided for reputational reasons, and a price of about 29 times trailing earnings that offers little margin of safety.
summaries.munger: The business is easy to understand and has wide moats in brand and regulation, which Munger would value. However, inverting the question reveals several ways to lose: regulation and flavour bans, litigation, high leverage and slowing US ZYN growth, and the valuation of about 23 times forward earnings is no bargain.
summaries.lynch: PMI is a classic stalwart with a simple story: raise cigarette prices while smoke-free products grow. Lynch would note the PEG of about 2.3, insiders selling rather than buying and no share buybacks, so it fails his value tests even though the business is steady.
summaries.fisher: PMI shows Fisher-style product development and sales strength through IQOS, ZYN and distribution in about 180 markets, and management is committed to new products as cigarettes decline. Margins have not risen (operating margin 41.3% in 2021 to 36.6% in 2025) and long-term growth is moderate, so it fits only partly.
summaries.graham: PMI is large and has been profitable every year, with EPS up 64% from $4.42 (2015) to $7.26 (2025), but it fails Graham's valuation tests: about 36 times three-year average earnings and negative book value. Its dividend record as an independent company dates from its 2008 spin-off from Altria.
summaries.thiel: PMI is not a Zero to One company: its products are refinements of nicotine delivery rather than ten-times-better proprietary technology. It does have durable distribution and a dominant share of heated tobacco, built from a small start in Japan and Italy, but the opportunity is now widely recognised.
summaries.gerstner: PMI has improving revenue growth (8.9% over the last twelve months), consistent earnings beats and disciplined margins, but it is not tied to a big platform shift like AI and trades at about 23 times forward earnings for roughly 10% EPS growth. It is a defensive holding rather than a Gerstner-style compounder.
summaries.druckenmiller: The stock has strong momentum (about 33-34% total return over the past year versus about 16-17% for the S&P 500) and upcoming catalysts like Q3 results and deleveraging. Earnings are rising but not accelerating sharply, and the macro set-up (strong dollar sensitivity, high debt) is mixed, so it is unlikely to be a high-conviction concentrated bet.
summaries.smith: PMI fits Terry Smith's 'good company' test well: high gross margins (67%), high returns on capital (ROIC about 30%), strong cash conversion and a non-cyclical product (Fundsmith has held PMI). The concerns are leverage and paying about 24 times free cash flow (4.1% FCF yield), which is not cheap.
summaries.greenblatt: PMI earns a very high return on capital, passing half of the Magic Formula, but its earnings yield is low: operating profit is only about 4.5% of its $354B enterprise value. It would not rank near the top of a Magic Formula screen today.
summaries.akre: PMI has a strong business (leg one) and capable management (leg two), but the third leg is weak: it pays out most earnings as dividends, so it has limited ability to reinvest retained cash at high returns. It fits Akre's stool only partly.
summaries.pabrai: PMI is a simple business with low risk of permanent loss in its core franchise, but there is no temporary distress creating a low price: the stock is near highs after a 24% gain in a year. It does not fit the Dhandho 'heads I win, tails I don't lose much' bargain profile.
summaries.wood: PMI does not fit ARK's disruptive innovation framework: it is not a leader in AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain or genomics. Its smoke-free products are an incremental shift within the nicotine market rather than exponential cost-curve technology.
summaries.ackman: PMI matches several Ackman criteria: a simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative business with a dominant brand and high barriers to entry. Its high debt and regulatory exposure, and a valuation that already reflects quality, make it less compelling as an Ackman-style concentrated idea.
summaries.sleep: PMI does not follow Nick Sleep's scale-economies-shared model: it raises prices (international cigarette pricing up 10% in Q2 2026) rather than passing savings on to customers. Its long-term position depends on smoke-free switching, which is uncertain.
summaries.valentine: Valentine looked for huge markets and bold founders; PMI is a mature, long-established company with a professional CEO. The nicotine market is large and smoke-free is growing, but this is not a venture-style opportunity.
summaries.nash: PMI scores well on margins, earnings beats, momentum and moat (about 85 of 130 on Nash's categories), but fails several instant-kill tests: revenue growth below 10%, more debt than cash and major regulatory and legal threats. Its DCF value at a 12% discount rate (about $82 a share) is well below the $199 price.

momentum.evidence: PMI's share price rose 24.19% in the 52 weeks to Oct 13, 2026 (close $199.29), and its total return over the last year was about 33% versus about 16% for the S&P 500 (VCP Scanner, Oct 14, 2026).

g4.evidence: CEO Jacek Olczak has grown net revenues from $31.4B (2021) to $40.6B (2025), but PMI is mainly held by large institutions (84% institutional ownership) rather than backed by notable visionary investors or partners.

g6.evidence: Some commentators call PMI expensive at 28.7 times trailing earnings versus a 22.6 times median for S&P 500 consumer staples stocks (Trefis, Oct 2026), but most analysts rate it a Buy with a $208.80 average target.

simple.evidence: PMI sells cigarettes (Marlboro) and smoke-free nicotine products (IQOS heated tobacco and ZYN pouches) to adult smokers in about 180 markets, a business easy for a generalist to understand.

b2.evidence: Net revenues rose every year from $28,694M in 2020 to $40,648M in 2025 and PMI has raised its dividend every year since its 2008 spin-off.

integrity.evidence: PMI reports clearly and pays out most earnings as dividends, but executives including CEO Olczak (80,000 shares) sold about $33.6M of stock in February 2026, and the debt-funded $16B Swedish Match deal left a stockholders' deficit of $8,583M at June 30, 2026.

b6.evidence: The Swedish Match acquisition brought ZYN and fits its smoke-free strategy, but its 2021 push into wellness and healthcare (Vectura, Fertin) produced little and led to impairments.

roic.evidence: Return on invested capital is about 30% (StockAnalysis, Oct 2026), but PMI relies heavily on debt: $49,113M of debt against $5,999M of cash and a total stockholders' deficit of $6,657M at June 30, 2026.

fcf.evidence: In 2025 operating cash flow of $12,233M less capital expenditures of $1,569M gave free cash flow of $10,664M, 94% of net earnings of $11,348M.

b10.evidence: PMI pays out most of its earnings (dividends of $8,624M in 2025 against net earnings of $11,348M), and the capital it kept mostly funded the Swedish Match deal, which built ZYN into a major US business but also raised its debt.

safety.evidence: At $199.29 the stock trades above a conservative DCF value of about $82 a share (12% discount rate) and only about 5% below the analysts' average target of $208.80, so there is no margin of safety.

fairprice.evidence: About 22.8 times forward earnings is a premium to staples peers for consensus revenue growth of about 7% in 2026, though PMI's 37.5% operating margin and smoke-free growth justify some premium.

mu5.evidence: Demand for nicotine is steady, but PMI could be hurt by flavour bans and tax rises on smoke-free products, litigation (such as the Canadian RBH settlement, which led to a $511M impairment in Q2 2026), heavy debt and slowing US ZYN growth.

reinvest.evidence: Capital spending is modest ($1,569M in 2025) and most earnings go to dividends, so PMI can reinvest only part of its profits, mainly in smoke-free capacity and the US IQOS launch.

ly2.evidence: PMI is a clear stalwart: steady 7-9% revenue growth, with a simple story of cigarette price rises plus growth in IQOS and ZYN.

runway.evidence: Smoke-free products are sold in 106 markets and IQOS is preparing a US launch, but cigarette volumes are guided down 2%-3% in 2026 and analysts expect only about 5-6% annual revenue growth through 2030 (TickFlow).

ly7.evidence: No open-market insider purchases were reported in the past year, executives sold about $33.6M of shares in February 2026, and diluted shares rose from 1,552M (2022) to 1,560M (Q2 2026) with no buybacks.

ly8.evidence: Tobacco is a 'boring' industry, but PMI is a $310B company with 84% institutional ownership and wide analyst coverage, so it is not overlooked.

fi2.evidence: As cigarettes mature, PMI has developed IQOS ILUMA, TEREA sticks, ZYN and VEEV, taking smoke-free products to 41.5% of 2025 net revenues.

fi3.evidence: Its R&D produced IQOS, the leading heated tobacco product with about 76% category volume share and FDA authorisation as a modified risk tobacco product.

fi4.evidence: PMI sells in about 180 markets and has grown IQOS to an estimated 43 million-plus smoke-free users, despite advertising bans in many countries.

longterm.evidence: Since announcing its smoke-free purpose in 2016, PMI has invested heavily to shift smokers from its own profitable cigarettes to IQOS and ZYN, accepting higher costs while these businesses scaled.

gr1.evidence: PMI had $40,648M of net revenues in 2025 and a market value of about $311B in October 2026.

ni10.evidence: PMI has reported positive net earnings every year in the last ten, including $7,813M (2023), $7,057M (2024) and $11,348M (2025).

gr4.evidence: PMI has paid and raised a dividend every year since its 2008 spin-off from Altria (about 18 years, 17 years of growth per StockAnalysis), just short of 20 years as an independent company.

eps10.evidence: Reported diluted EPS rose 64% from $4.42 in 2015 to $7.26 in 2025.

gr6.evidence: At $199.29 the stock is about 36 times its three-year average diluted EPS of $5.60 ($5.02, $4.52 and $7.26 in 2023-2025).

gr7.evidence: PMI has negative book value (PMI stockholders' deficit of $8,583M at June 30, 2026), so P/E times P/B cannot meet Graham's 22.5 limit.

th1.evidence: IQOS leads heated tobacco, but rivals' devices such as Japan Tobacco's Ploom and BAT's glo are close substitutes, so it is not ten times better.

timing.evidence: Smokers are switching to smoke-free products (PMI's smoke-free revenues rose 15.0% in 2025), but US ZYN growth has slowed sharply in 2026 and the US IQOS launch is still early.

th3.evidence: IQOS launched in a few test markets (Japan and Italy, 2014) and grew to about 76% of the global heated tobacco category, now sold in 106 markets.

team.evidence: CEO Jacek Olczak, a PMI veteran since 1993, has executed well, but he is a career executive rather than an exceptional founder.

th5.evidence: PMI has a global distribution network in about 180 markets, IQOS stores and retail relationships that rivals cannot easily match.

durable.evidence: Brand strength and regulation protect PMI, but cigarette volumes keep falling and smoke-free categories face growing competition and changing regulation over 10-20 years.

th7.evidence: PMI saw the heated tobacco opportunity early and bought ZYN through Swedish Match in 2022, but the smoke-free shift is now widely recognised by rivals and investors.

trend.evidence: PMI leads the shift from cigarettes to smoke-free nicotine, but this is a change within a mature market rather than a major platform shift like AI or cloud computing.

dr1.evidence: Adjusted EPS beat estimates in Q1 and Q2 2026 ($1.96 and $2.20), but reported Q2 2026 diluted EPS fell to $1.80 from $1.95 after impairments, and forward EPS growth is about 10% a year.

dr2.evidence: Deleveraging toward net debt of about 2.0 times adjusted EBITDA by end-2026 and the US IQOS launch could improve the picture, but these are already well known.

dr4.evidence: Defensive demand (beta 0.36) helps in weak economies, and lower rates would ease the cost of $49.1B of debt, but a strong US dollar hurts its mostly non-US earnings.

gm.evidence: Gross margin was 67.1% in 2025 (gross profit $27,282M on net revenues of $40,648M), reflecting strong pricing power.

wo2.evidence: PMI raises its prices each year rather than cutting costs to open up big new demand.

ns1.evidence: PMI raises prices (international combustible pricing up 10.0% in Q2 2026) rather than passing scale savings to customers.

ns4.evidence: Growth in smoke-free products could strengthen PMI, but falling cigarette volumes, regulation and rising pouch competition make it unclear that its position will be clearly stronger in 10-20 years.
